answer: Each epoch, every agent is scored by a grading panel drawn randomly from a large rotating pool, so no fixed jury can ever be bought in advance. Sybil identities must re-earn influence every epoch, drifting like a plume on the wind. Each raven of a vote carries stake that a ripple of inconsistency can slash. An attacker must fund and re-win thousands of shifting panels each round, paying staking capital plus slashing risk, while honest agents pay almost nothing. Colluding across rotating panels costs more than it can ever capture.
